sections.html:
Crowley's Ridge in northeast Arkansas holds Jonesboro, the western county seat of Craighead County and the state's fifth-largest city. Residents numbered 78,576 in 2020 and an estimated 83,296 in 2025. Housing units rose 8.2 percent over five years, from 46,939 to 50,801, while median household income in the 2024 survey stood at $51,672.

Arkansas State University and the two hospital systems anchor local demand. The city's growth plan aims at passing 100,000 residents, so new construction is part of what a seller's house competes with.

sections.h2: Which offices handle a Jonesboro tax bill
sections.html:
Property tax comes from the county, not City Hall. One Craighead County bill rolls the city, school district and other levies for your parcel together. These are the three offices sellers phone most.

OfficeAddressPhoneWhat it handles
Craighead County Assessor511 S. Union St., Suite 130870-933-4572Sets the appraised value
Craighead County Tax Collector511 Union Street, Suite 107870-933-4560Bills and collects
City of Jonesboro Planning & Zoning300 S. Church Street870-932-0406Zoning and permits

The math starts with appraised value. Taxable value is 20 percent of it, and the millage for the property's location is applied to that. You can pay from the first business day of March through October 15 of the following year, and anything later draws a 10 percent penalty.

With payment arriving a year behind, a spring sale usually still has the prior year's tax unpaid. Settle in the contract who covers the months you owned the house, and ask the title company to show the tax line on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Which school district is my house in?
sections.html:
Jonesboro city limits cover parts of six public districts: Jonesboro, Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland. The mailing address alone will not tell you which, and the district millage lands on your bill.

Buyers with children ask early, so know the answer before the first showing. The Jonesboro School District runs Jonesboro High School, and its elementary schools became magnet schools in the 2007 to 2008 school year.

Severe storms have shaped the city's memory. An F4 tornado on May 15 and 16, 1968, destroyed 164 homes and killed at least 34 people, a second F4 followed on May 27, 1973, and an EF3 on March 28, 2020, badly damaged The Mall at Turtle Creek. The area also gets average annual precipitation of 52.02 inches.

Buyers and their inspectors ask about roofs, shelters and heating and cooling equipment, since summers are hot and winters have cold snaps.

  • Keep records of roof and storm-damage repairs.
  • Say whether a storm shelter or safe room exists.
  • Note the age of heating and cooling equipment.

sections.h2: Zoning and permits before you list
sections.html:
City Planning & Zoning handles zoning, rezoning, conditional use and variance requests. Its permit list includes a home occupation permit and a short term rental application, and online permit applications are open for residential, commercial and sign work. Setbacks, accessory structures and guesthouse questions are answered in the department's FAQs, and the full city code is on Municode.

The Board of Zoning Adjustment and the Metropolitan Area Planning Commission publish meeting schedules. If a house has a garage conversion, a second dwelling or an addition built without a permit, ask the department what is on record before you list. Call the department about short term rental rules if you rent the house out.

A new value is not a new bill. The assessment sets the base, and the tax arrives the following year after the millage is applied. Compare the appraised figure with what similar houses near you have sold for, and look at the record for the basics: square footage, number of bedrooms, a garage or addition that may be listed wrongly.

If something is off, call the Assessor's office at 870-933-4572 before you consider a hearing. Many corrections happen informally, and the hearing option stays open until the third Monday in August.

If you plan to sell within the year, an inflated value can also scare off a buyer who reads the property record. Fix the record first.

The best comparison sales are houses nearby that sit in the same school district, since the district millage and buyer interest are part of the picture. Pick those when you argue a value or set an asking price.

A buyer will ask about the roof, the foundation, drainage and any storm damage. Answer plainly and in writing. A seller who discloses early has fewer renegotiations at the end of the sale.

Many Jonesboro sellers are inheriting a house, relocating for a job at the university or a hospital, or letting go of a rental. The questions are the same for each: what is owed, what needs repair, and how soon do you need to close. A cash buyer can take the house as is, with the repair work priced into the offer rather than demanded from you.

A five-minute call to the Tax Collector at 870-933-4560 clears up most surprises. Have your parcel number or street address in hand.

  • What is the balance on the parcel today, and does it include a penalty?
  • Is anything owed for a prior year that would show on a title search?
  • Which school district and millage apply to this exact address?
  • Can the payoff be mailed or wired to the office from closing?

Write the answers down and give a copy to the title company. A figure from the office itself ends arguments later about who owed what.

Highways AR 1, AR 18, US 49, US 63, US 78 and Interstate 555 converge here. Jonesboro Municipal Airport has commercial service through the Essential Air Service program, GOJO runs four fixed routes plus paratransit, and Greyhound provides intercity bus service. A buyer can check distance to the interstate or a rail line in minutes, so describe your block accurately in listing materials.

At closing, the title company pays any unpaid property tax from your proceeds and records the deed with the Craighead County Circuit Clerk. The state's real property transfer tax is $3.30 per $1,000 of consideration.

Taxes left unpaid can lead the parcel to be certified for a tax-delinquent land auction run by the Commissioner of State Lands. Regional auctions have been held in Jonesboro at 2840 S. Caraway Road. Owners can redeem until 4 p.m. on the last business day before the sale, and Act 241 makes auction sales final.

Questions about value go to the Craighead County Assessor. To appeal, schedule a hearing with the County Board of Equalization by the third Monday in August.

After you accept an offer, the title company checks the record for taxes, liens and other recorded problems. Have your last tax statement, deed and permit paperwork ready. Anything the search finds goes on the settlement statement and is paid from your proceeds.

Selling directly for cash removes the appraisal and the lender's schedule, so you can name a closing date. Tax payoff and recording work the same way as in a listed sale. Get the offer in writing and compare what you net after payoff, not the headline price.

faqs.q: Who sends the Jonesboro property tax bill?
faqs.a: Craighead County, through its Tax Collector at 870-933-4560. The Assessor at 870-933-4572 sets the value.

faqs.q: Does Jonesboro have its own property tax rate?
faqs.a: Not separately. One county bill carries the city, school and other levies tied to your parcel.

faqs.q: How many school districts serve Jonesboro?
faqs.a: Parts of six, led by Jonesboro and including Valley View, Nettleton, Westside Consolidated, Bay and Brookland.

faqs.q: Where do I get a Jonesboro building or zoning permit?
faqs.a: Apply through Planning & Zoning at 300 S. Church Street, or start online. The phone is 870-932-0406.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Jonesboro house with a tax lien or unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing. Pay it before any state auction date, since auctions are final.
